children.text: The city has lost its connection with a lot of volunteers due to the COVID pandemic. There is a shortage of daily care workers available to assist senior citizens who need support.

attributesChanged.text: <Summarize the rationale for the new product. Provide a general description of the history or situation that leads to the recognition that this product should be built.>

children.text: Situation The city faces an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 senior cases needing assistance, as well as elementary students who need dedicated coaching.

attributesChanged.text: Situation       Describe the background, context, and environment.

children.text: Problem The current manual volunteer assignment process takes approximately two weeks because of the manual data submissions for police checks. There is also no centralized system to track demand against available volunteers.

attributesChanged.text: Problem        Describe the business problem (or problems) as you now understand it

children.text: Implication The lack of a centralized tracking system results in unexpected volunteer shortages and prevents the city from properly planning.

attributesChanged.text: Implication    Describe the likely results if the problem isn’t solved.

children.text: Benefit A centralized system will allow the city to accurately match volunteers to cases, provide wellness checks, and offer remote tutoring to elementary students.

attributesChanged.text: Benefit           State the business value of solving the problem.

children.text: Vision A reliable, automated system that forecasts daily needs, prevents volunteer shortages, and creates a mutually beneficial platform for the community and local businesses.

attributesChanged.text: Vision            Describe what the desired future state would look like.>

children.text:
• Track 60% of the city’s senior cases within the system during its first year of operation.
  • Provide volunteer support to 85% of the reported senior cases within the first year.
  • Reduce the volunteer assignment timeframe to 30% of its current duration, ensuring seniors receive support within three days.
  • Increase business transactions in the Downtown area and at local shop s by 10% using engagement activities to lower the crime rate.

attributesChanged.text: <Describe the important business objectives of the product in a way that is quantitative and measurable. Focus on the value provided to the business, including estimates of revenue or cost savings, return on investment analysis, or target release dates.>

· Provide volunteer support to 85% of the reported senior cases within the first year.

· Reduce the volunteer assignment timeframe to 30% of its current duration, ensuring seniors receive support within three days.

· Increase business transactions in the Downtown area and at local shop s by 10% using engagement activities to lower the crime rate.

attributesChanged.text: <Summarize the major business risks associated with developing this product, such as marketplace competition, timing issues, user acceptance, implementation issues, or possible negative impacts on the business. Estimate the severity of the risks and identify any risk mitigation actions that could be taken.>

· A sudden shortage of volunteers could disrupt services if the system fails to accurately predict need.

· The government automated background check system is currently under testing, any delays in this could delay the goal of processing background checks within 48 hours.

children.text:
• Assumption 1: Engaging volunteers in activities will reduce the city crime rate and will subsequently boost the downtown business by 10%.
  • Assumption 2: Local business owners will act as sponsors by offering promotions and incentives to motivate the volunteers.
  • Dependency 1: The project relies on the government’s new background check system becoming available to automate police certificate processing within 48 hours.
  • Dependency 2: Volunteers assigned to elementary students must possess minimum educational skills and successfully pass a police certificate check.

attributesChanged.text: <Record any assumptions that were made when conceiving the project and preparing this document. Note any major dependencies the project must rely upon for success, such as specific technologies, third-party vendors, development partners, or other business relationships.>

· Assumption 1: Engaging volunteers in activities will reduce the city crime rate and will subsequently boost the downtown business by 10%.

· Assumption 2: Local business owners will act as sponsors by offering promotions and incentives to motivate the volunteers.

· Dependency 1: The project relies on the government’s new background check system becoming available to automate police certificate processing within 48 hours.

· Dependency 2: Volunteers assigned to elementary students must possess minimum educational skills and successfully pass a police certificate check.

children.text:
• F-1: Centralized Case Management & Intake: Intake, categorize, and track care requests for seniors (daily check-in calls, wellness education) and elementary students (specialized tutoring/coaching).

  • F-2: Volunteer Onboarding & Qualification Vetting: Volunteer self-registration portal capturing personal records, educational credentials for youth coaching, and automated background check submissions.

  • F-3: Background Check Gateway Integration: Real-time data interchange with the Government Automated Police Clearance Service.

  • F-4: Matching & Rapid Dispatch Engine: Rule-based matching engine pairing verified volunteers with open cases based on skills, geography, and availability within 3 days. 

  • F-5: Predictive Demand Forecasting & Shortage Notification: Daily automated projection engine alerting city coordinators to forecasted demand spikes and volunteer deficits for the following 7 days.

  • F-6: Community Sponsor & Volunteer Reward Module: Portal for local downtown retailers to post promotional discounts, coupons, and incentives for active volunteers.

attributesChanged.text: <Include a numbered list of the major features of the new product, emphasizing those features  that distinguish it from previous or competing products. Specific user requirements and functional requirements developed later may be traced back to these features.>

• F-1: Centralized Case Management & Intake: Intake, categorize, and track care requests for seniors (daily check-in calls, wellness education) and elementary students (specialized tutoring/coaching).

  • F-2: Volunteer Onboarding & Qualification Vetting: Volunteer self-registration portal capturing personal records, educational credentials for youth coaching, and automated background check submissions.

  • F-3: Background Check Gateway Integration: Real-time data interchange with the Government Automated Police Clearance Service.

  • F-4: Matching & Rapid Dispatch Engine: Rule-based matching engine pairing verified volunteers with open cases based on skills, geography, and availability within 3 days. 

  • F-5: Predictive Demand Forecasting & Shortage Notification: Daily automated projection engine alerting city coordinators to forecasted demand spikes and volunteer deficits for the following 7 days.

  • F-6: Community Sponsor & Volunteer Reward Module: Portal for local downtown retailers to post promotional discounts, coupons, and incentives for active volunteers.

children.text:
Initial release will focus on establishing core operations to resolve the senior care crisis: 

  • Senior case intake and lifecycle tracking (targeting 60% coverage). 

  • Volunteer registration, profile management, and basic qualification checks. 

  • Integration with the Automated Background Check System (48-hour Service Level Agreement). 

  • Core volunteer-to-senior assignment module achieving the 3-day turnaround. 

  • Daily automated notification engine warning municipal coordinators of 7-day forecasted shortages.

children.text:
• Release 2.0: Elementary student tutoring module (intake of student cases, vetting of volunteer academic credentials, and pairing with minors).

  • Release 2.5: Sponsor loyalty and promotion engine allowing local businesses to redeem promotional codes for volunteers.

  • Release 3.0: Advanced machine learning forecasting models and mobile applications for volunteers to log call outcomes and wellness check notes.

attributesChanged.text: <If a staged evolution of the product is envisioned over time, indicate which major features will be deferred to later releases.>

children.text:
• EX-1: Direct Healthcare Provision: The system coordinates non-medical care (daily calls, wellness education) and coaching; it does not track or deliver clinical medical treatments, prescription management, or emergency 911 dispatch.

  • EX-2: Full Primary Online Schooling: The platform is not an online Learning Management System (LMS) or video classroom; students continue utilizing primary school platforms, with VMS managing supplemental coaching assignments only.

  • EX-3: Internal Background Check Processing: The VMS will not adjudicate or compute criminal records internally; it delegates all background verifications to external government law enforcement APIs.

children.text: Before deployment of the volunteer management system, the system must be able to have multiple interfaces for different users. The volunteers will need to be able to send information (eg. For criminal record checks and other personal information) to the monitors of the system as well as show volunteer work opportunities available. The monitors of the system should be the only ones who receive forecasted information and admin management capabilities. This will also work as the Main system and will be where all centralized information is located. Any “costumers/clients” using the system should be able to see availability of volunteers and see their previous experience or qualification levels for choosing a volunteer. Each interface will require clean and simple navigation will clear controls for navigating the system. Security of personal information will be paramount in the development of the system because there continues to be cases of information leaks from applications and systems similar to this one. The system will be for the city only starting with Kamloops.
